fixed_statement: Let \(T\in \Dr_2\) contain \(V_{L_1}\). The rank \(2\) tropical linear space \(T\) must possess an infinite ray where \(x_1,x_2,x_3\to\infty\) simultaneously. In the initial matroid of \(T\) at infinity, the subset \(\{1,2,3\}\) must act globally as a single parallel class, or contain loops alongside a parallel class. If \(T\) contains loops, their union must form a valid flat of \(F_7\); the all-loop case is not a rank \(2\) case.
fixed_proof: By the coordinate description of \(V_{L_1}\) in Proposition 2, containment of \(V_{L_1}\) requires the simultaneous boundary direction \(e_{123}\). This structural limit mandates that, in the initial matroid of \(T\) at infinity, the subset \(\{1,2,3\}\) must act globally as a single parallel class, or contain loops alongside a parallel class. The listed alternatives are the corresponding initial-matroid possibilities for realizing that direction. If \(T\) contains loops, their union must form a valid flat of \(F_7\), hence has size \(0,1,3\), or \(7\); the all-loop case is not a rank \(2\) case.
